crime_highlights: Mr. Klein came up behind E.I. and stabbed her four times with a large hunting knife before she escaped, though seriously injured
Mr. Klein then turned upon Ms. Reimer, and stabbed her a total of 14 times
tragically she slipped away not long afterwards
E.I. survived her injuries, but, as I will explain, the consequences have been extreme and are long-lasting.
rationale_highlights: many of these are apparent in Mr. Klein's circumstances, including his loss of family, community, and language and culture
also mitigating are the Gladue factors I noted earlier, in reviewing Mr. Klein's background and character
The Gladue factors undoubtedly made it harder for Mr. Klein to succeed in life.
note: Gladue treated as mitigating; effect on parole ineligibility stated in para 75.

crime_highlights: Mr. P. offered K.V.P. $600 to sleep with him, which she did not
Mr. P. also started giving her change and later $20 bills in exchange for hugs.
He would sometimes babysit K.V.P. and N.R.P. when their mother was working and stay overnight.
rationale_highlights: Mr. P.'s parents were both residential school victims.

I must at the same time take into account the sentencing regime in place at the time of the offences, the passage of time without reoffending, his aboriginal background, and the systemic factors present which were previously recognized and now found in s. 718(2)(e) of the Code.
The court must consider to what extent systemic and background factors related to aboriginal offenders explain the commission of the offence and the moral culpability of the offender.
